chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah and Ma'mar ibn Yahya and Isma'il al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no recitation in the funeral prayer, nor a fixed supplication; you may supplicate as it seems fit to you, and the deceased most deserving of a believer's supplication is [any deceased], and one should begin with the prayer upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)."
As for what he mentioned (may Allah have mercy on him) that he raises his hands with the Takbir in the first [Takbir] and does not raise them in the remaining Takbirat, he has narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for recitation and supplication during the Islamic funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the flexibility of Salat al-Mayyit by confirming the absence of fixed recitations or specific supplications, thereby granting the pray-er discretion in their du'a. It further highlights the hierarchical precedence of invoking blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and clarifies the ritual practice of raising hands only during the initial Takbir, a detail supported by subsequent reports in the text.
